headline: The Drywall Finisher Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet the crew, give measurements and times, describe the mud and the walls, ask for tools and materials, ask simple questions and ask for help, and start Drywall Finisher Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Pronounce Spanish sounds in drywall tool names and greet the crew and the contractor.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent in tool words; greetings

words.note: ll sounds like y in yes: YAH-nah.
ch as in church. Common Mexican word for the mud pan.
j is a strong h sound: HOON-tah.
LEE-hah; the j sounds like a strong h.
qu sounds like k: es-KEE-nah.
Short, clear vowels: pah-RED, stress on the last syllable.
The accent marks the stress: es-PAH-too-lah.
Trill the rr; the ll sounds like y.
A single r is a quick tap; ll sounds like y.
A woman is la ayudante.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Carlos.
Nice to meet you, I'm the new helper.
words.es: Mucho gusto, soy el ayudante nuevo.
words.note: A woman says: soy la ayudante nueva.
Formal usted: use it with the contractor or the homeowner.

words.en: How do you say "trowel" in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a crew member, say your name and that you are the new helper, and ask how to say trowel in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Count to 1,000, tell the time, and give drywall measurements in feet, inches, sheets and buckets.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and feet, inches, sheets, rolls and buckets

words.note: Plural pies: 10 pies.
Also el panel or la tablaroca; many US crews just say el drywall.
Mexican and US word for bucket.

words.es: La pared mide 10 pies y 6 pulgadas.

words.en: We start at 7 in the morning.
words.es: Empezamos a las 7 de la mañana.

words.note: Use son las for every hour except 1: es la 1.

lessons.speaking: Tell the foreman what time you start, how long a wall measures, and how many sheets and buckets you need.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what something is and how it is: the mud is wet, the wall is smooth, he is the painter.
lessons.focus: ser for who or what something is, estar for the condition of mud and walls or a location

words.note: Agrees: la pasta está seca.
Agrees: la pared está mojada.
Common on Mexican crews; agrees: la pared está pareja.
A woman is la pintora.
A woman is la contratista. The GC is el contratista general.
A woman says acabadora. Drywall is the usual loanword on US crews.
ser: who someone is.
estar: a condition that can change.

words.en: The tools are in the truck.
words.es: Las herramientas están en la troca.
words.note: estar for location. Troca is the common US word for truck.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member who you are, whether the mud is wet or dry, and where the tools are.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, what there is, and what you need on the job, like mud, tape and screws.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer, and hay que + infinitive for what must be done

words.note: The common word for joint compound; you also hear el compuesto or el mud.
Feminine noun, but it takes el in the singular: el agua fría.

words.en: I need a box of screws.

words.note: Informal tú, between coworkers.

words.en: There are 3 corner beads in the truck.
You have to wear a dust mask to sand.
words.es: Hay que usar mascarilla para lijar.
words.note: Hay que + infinitive: something everyone must do.

words.en: Do you want texture on the ceiling?
words.note: Formal usted, for the homeowner or the contractor.

words.en: You have to mix the mud well.
words.es: Hay que mezclar bien la pasta.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you have and what you need for taping, and ask if they have mesh tape.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do, and what you can do today on the job.
lessons.focus: ir and ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer for doing a task, poder for can

words.note: Mano means a coat of mud or paint: dar una mano.
Indoors it means ceiling; outdoors, roof. In Mexico you also hear el plafón.

words.en: I'm going to the supply house.
words.es: Voy a la tienda de materiales.

words.en: Tomorrow we're going to put on the second coat.
words.es: Mañana vamos a dar la segunda mano.
words.note: ir a + infinitive for a plan.

words.en: Today we're doing the kitchen ceiling.
words.es: Hoy hacemos el techo de la cocina.

words.en: I'm going to finish the bathroom first.
words.es: Voy a terminar el baño primero.

words.note: Informal tú, between coworkers.

lessons.speaking: Tell your foreman where you are going and what you are going to do next, and ask if you can use the ladder.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Describe daily drywall work with present-tense verbs: I sand, we cover, they sweep.
lessons.focus: Regular -ar, -er and -ir present endings for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: Many US crews also say el primer.
lijar: yo lijo, tú lijas, nosotros lijamos.

words.en: You fill the hole with mud.
words.es: Usted tapa el hoyo con pasta.

words.en: We cover the floor with plastic.
words.es: Nosotros cubrimos el piso con plástico.
words.note: -ir verb cubrir: nosotros cubrimos.

words.en: They sweep up the dust at the end of the day.
words.es: Ellos barren el polvo al final del día.
words.note: -er verb barrer: ellos barren.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you do each day on the job: what you sand, what you cover, and who cleans up the dust.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask simple questions on the job site: where, who, when, how many, how, why and which.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué and cuál, with ¿ and ?

words.note: Agrees with the noun: ¿cuántas hojas?, ¿cuántos tornillos?
Two words for why; porque, one word, means because.
Many US crews also say el foreman.

words.en: Which one is the lightweight mud?

lessons.speaking: Ask a new crew member who the foreman is, where the trowel is, and when the material arrives.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, nothing and not yet, and ask for more, less or another on the job.
lessons.focus: Negatives no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, and amounts más, menos, otro

words.note: Use no before the verb: no hay nada.
Use no before the verb: no veo a nadie.
Never put un before it: otra cubeta.
A bubble or blister under the tape.

words.es: La pasta todavía no está seca.

words.en: I never sand without a dust mask.

words.es: No hay nadie en el cuarto.

words.en: I need another bucket of mud.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker the mud is not dry yet, that you need another bucket, and that one joint needs more mud.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask politely with ¿Puede…? and give simple usted commands to a helper or homeowner.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede + infinitive? for polite requests, and usted commands: ponga, espere, llame

words.en: Can you open the window, please?
Can you pass me the taping knife?
Please put painter's tape on the door.
words.es: Ponga cinta de pintor en la puerta, por favor.
Tire la basura afuera, por favor.

words.note: Use the personal a before a person: a + el = al.

lessons.speaking: Ask a helper politely to open the window and pass you the taping knife, then tell them to call the foreman.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize cognates like inspección and humedad, and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, and survival phrases for getting help

words.note: Moisture or dampness in a wall, not only humid air.
A woman is la clienta.
Masculine even though it ends in -a.

words.en: I don't understand, can you repeat that, please?

words.es: Hay humedad detrás de la pared.

lessons.speaking: Tell the foreman there is moisture behind a wall, say you don't understand the answer, and ask them to repeat it slowly.
